stories.headline: Anthropic in talks to buy world-model startup Decart for about $6B ahead of its IPO

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is in talks to acquire AI startup Decart AI for about $6 billion; the deal has not been finalized and talks could fall through, Bloomberg reported on August 12-13, 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic PBC is in talks to buy the artificial intelligence startup Decart AI for about $6 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. The deal has not been finalized and talks could fall through.

key_facts.fact: Decart works with AI developers to maximize performance across a wide range of chips and builds generative video 'world models' capable of modifying live video feeds instantly
key_facts.excerpt: Decart works with AI developers to help them maximize performance from a wide range of chips. It also focuses on generative video, using so-called world models capable of modifying live video feeds instantly.

key_facts.fact: If completed, Decart's team would join Anthropic's inference and performance organization, and the deal would help Anthropic absorb growing demand ahead of its public listing
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is in an early stage, and if completed, Decart's team would join Anthropic's inference and performance organization, the source added.

key_facts.fact: Decart raised $300 million in May in a round led by Radical Ventures with Nvidia joining as a new investor; the round valued it at nearly $4 billion, up from $3.1 billion in August 2025
key_facts.excerpt: The funding round valued Decart at nearly $4 billion, according to the Wall Street Journal, up from $3.1 billion in August 2025. A potential $6 billion acquisition would therefore represent a significant premium over its latest reported valuation.

key_facts.fact: A $6 billion purchase would be Anthropic's largest known deal; the company has been cautious about large acquisitions but is spending heavily on compute capacity
key_facts.excerpt: If completed, the acquisition would be Anthropic's largest known deal and would come as the AI company prepares for a potential initial public offering (IPO). Anthropic has generally been cautious about large acquisitions but has been spending heavily on computing capacity.

key_facts.fact: The report follows Israeli media claims days earlier that Elon Musk's SpaceX was in talks to buy Decart for several billion dollars, which Musk publicly denied on Monday night
key_facts.excerpt: The report comes days after Israeli media reported that Elon Musk's SpaceX was in talks to acquire Decart for several billion dollars. Musk publicly denied the report Monday night.

stories.headline: Anthropic investors target a $2T October IPO, the largest listing in history

key_facts.fact: Anthropic investors expect the company to go public in October at a valuation of $2 trillion or more, which would be the largest IPO in history, according to the Financial Times
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic investors expect the AI company to go public in October at a valuation of $2 trillion or more, which would make it the largest initial public offering in history, according to the Financial Times.

key_facts.fact: Half a dozen backers said annualized revenue should land between $100 billion and $120 billion before year-end, more than tenfold the $47 billion reported in May
key_facts.excerpt: Half a dozen of Anthropic's backers said that the Claude maker's annualized revenue is expected to land somewhere between $100 billion and $120 billion before the year closes — a figure that would represent growth of more than tenfold compared with the $47 billion annualized revenue the company reported in May.

key_facts.fact: A $2 trillion debut would surpass SpaceX, which went public at a $1.77 trillion valuation in June, and would double Anthropic's last private mark of $965 billion post-money
key_facts.excerpt: Such a figure would surpass SpaceX, which went public at a $1.77 trillion valuation in June... The company last raised capital at a $965 billion post-money valuation.

key_facts.fact: One investor argued a company growing 800% a year merits at least a 30-times-revenue multiple, implying roughly $3 trillion; Palantir and Nebius have traded near 55 times sales this year
key_facts.excerpt: One investor said that a company expanding at 800% annually would, at the very low end of reasonable expectations, command a 30-times-revenue multiple — implying a $3 trillion valuation for Anthropic. AI-adjacent names such as Palantir and Nebius have changed hands this year at multiples near 55 times their sales.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic filed a draft registration statement with the SEC in early June, kicking off a US listing process ahead of rival OpenAI, days after closing a $65 billion Series H at a $965 billion valuation
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has submitted a draft registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission, officially kicking off the process for a US IPO and teeing the AI lab up for a potential listing in autumn – ahead of its biggest rival OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's annualized revenue was roughly $20 billion at the start of 2026 and $47 billion in May; on $100 billion of exit revenue, a $2 trillion valuation implies about 20 times forward sales
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's annualized revenue stood at approximately $20 billion at the beginning of 2026 and rose to $47 billion in May, with investors projecting its ARR to double and surge to $100 billion–$120 billion by the end of 2026. Based on an estimated $100 billion revenue by the end of 2026, a $2 trillion valuation implies a forward price-to-sales ratio of just 20x.

stories.headline: DeepSeek quietly ships V4-Pro-0813, its flagship out of preview at $0.435/$0.87 per 1M tokens

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek swapped its flagship endpoint to the 0813 build on Wednesday, August 12, with no blog post or announcement; the only tell was the model version on its API pricing page reading DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek shipped the finished version of its flagship on Wednesday with no blog post and no announcement. The tell was a table cell: the model version listed for 'deepseek-v4-pro' on the API pricing page now reads DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813.

key_facts.fact: The GA build ends a preview that ran since April 24, 2026; OpenRouter listed the model on August 12 as 'the GA release of DeepSeek V4 Pro'
key_facts.excerpt: OpenRouter lists the model dated 12 August 2026, describing it verbatim as 'a large-scale mixture-of-experts model from DeepSeek. This is the GA release of DeepSeek V4 Pro.'

key_facts.fact: Pricing is $0.435 per million input tokens on a cache miss, $0.003625 on a cache hit and $0.87 per million output tokens, with a 1M-token context window, 384K max output and a concurrency limit of 500
key_facts.excerpt: | PRICING(1) | 1M INPUT TOKENS (CACHE HIT) | $0.0028 | $0.003625 | | | 1M INPUT TOKENS (CACHE MISS) | $0.14 | $0.435 | | | 1M OUTPUT TOKENS | $0.28 | $0.87 | | Concurrency Limit(2) | | 2500 | 500 |

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's own comparison chart claims large agent gains over its preview build: Terminal Bench 2.1 from 72.1 to 87.9, CyberGym 52.7 to 83.3 and DeepSWE 12.8 to 62.7
key_facts.excerpt: Terminal Bench 2.1 rising from 72.1 to 87.9, CyberGym from 52.7 to 83.3, and DeepSWE from 12.8 to 62.7 — a gain of 49.9 percentage points — each measured against the company's own V4 Pro Preview, not against a competitor.

key_facts.fact: Across nine agent benchmarks where both are scored, DeepSeek's table puts Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 ahead by an average of 5.3%, while Fable 5 costs $10/$50 per million tokens — roughly 46 times V4 Pro's blended $0.65
key_facts.excerpt: Across nine agent benchmarks where both models are scored, DeepSeek's table puts Claude Fable 5 ahead by an average of 5.3%... On blended rates that's $30 against $0.65—roughly 46 times, or 4,600% of the cost.

key_facts.fact: No independent lab has benchmarked the 0813 build, open weights for it have not been published and DeepSeek's changelog carries no entry for the release
key_facts.excerpt: benchable.ai's page for the model shows an empty benchmark section — no third-party results at all. DeepSeek's official changelog contains no entry for the release. Open weights for the 0813 build have not been published.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek will move to peak/off-peak billing from 16:00 UTC on August 16, with peak V4-Pro rates of $1.32 input and $3.96 output per million tokens — roughly triple the current list price
key_facts.excerpt: The new prices take effect at 16:00 UTC on August 16, 2026... | deepseek-v4-pro | OFF-PEAK | $0.022 | $0.66 | $1.98 | | PEAK | $0.044 | $1.32 | $3.96 |

stories.headline: Jeff Dean's week-old Discovery Loop in talks for $1B at a roughly $10B valuation

key_facts.fact: Jeff Dean has been in discussions for $1 billion in financing at a valuation of around $10 billion for his new AI startup, Discovery Loop, people familiar told Business Insider
key_facts.excerpt: The legendary Google engineer has been in discussions for $1 billion in financing at a valuation of around $10 billion for his new AI startup, Discovery Loop, people familiar with the matter told Business Insider.

key_facts.fact: Dean, who spent 27 years at Google, described Discovery Loop on X as a public benefit corporation whose mission is 'to automate machine learning, science, and engineering to accelerate discoveries and progress'
key_facts.excerpt: Dean has been open about the goal of the startup, Discovery Loop, describing it on X as a public benefit corporation 'whose mission is to automate machine learning, science, and engineering to accelerate discoveries and progress.'

key_facts.fact: Discovery Loop was announced on August 5 by Dean together with Google veterans Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le and Oriol Vinyals
key_facts.excerpt: Other founding members include fellow Google veterans and scientists including Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le, and Oriol Vinyals.

key_facts.fact: The initial round was co-led by Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures, with Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed and Doerr Capital participating; Alphabet signed on as founding investor and cloud partner
key_facts.excerpt: The company has received financial support from a number of different sources, including Google's parent company Alphabet. The initial funding round is being co-led by Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures. Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed, and Doerr Capital also participated.

key_facts.fact: The talks value a company with no product, no customers and no revenue, formed only days earlier; the plan is AI that can run thousands of experiments in parallel
key_facts.excerpt: Business Insider reported this week that Dean is in talks for roughly $1 billion in new financing at a valuation near $10 billion. No product exists yet. No customers. No revenue. The number reflects belief in the team more than any tangible progress.

key_facts.fact: Dean or the company have not confirmed the figures, and a representative for Dean declined to comment on fundraising specifics
key_facts.excerpt: Dean or the company have not confirmed those numbers, and a representative for Dean had no comment about the fundraising talks.

stories.headline: Hassabis pitched an IAEA-style AI safety body to US officials before leaving DeepMind's CEO job

key_facts.fact: Demis Hassabis held discussions with government officials and leaders of other AI labs about forming a new independent industry safety entity in the weeks before he relinquished the Google DeepMind CEO role
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet's top scientist, Demis Hassabis, held discussions with government officials and leaders of other artificial-intelligence labs about forming a new independent industry safety entity in the weeks before he relinquished his role as chief executive of Google DeepMind, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: In discussions with peers, Hassabis likened the proposed organization to the International Atomic Energy Agency, and has been spending increasing amounts of time on an entity that would codify safety guardrails and best practices for developing AGI
key_facts.excerpt: Hassabis... has been spending increasing amounts of his time advancing the idea of an organization that would codify safety guardrails and best practices for developing artificial general intelligence, or AGI... he has likened the proposed entity to the International Atomic Energy Agency.

key_facts.fact: Hassabis first made the case publicly on July 14 in a post titled 'A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age', proposing a standards body modeled on FINRA, the industry-funded watchdog that polices US brokerages under SEC oversight
key_facts.excerpt: Titled 'A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age,' the post makes the case for a 'standards body' modeled after the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), which could test frontier models and develop best practices for their release.

key_facts.fact: Under the proposal, frontier labs would voluntarily share models with the body for review up to 30 days before release, with the test becoming mandatory for US deployment once the protocol proves effective
key_facts.excerpt: 'Initially, Frontier Labs would voluntarily share models with the Standards Body for review up to 30 days before release,' the post reads. 'Once the assessment protocol is shown to be effective and robust, formalisation could quickly follow, meaning that Frontier Models would be required to pass it to be deployed in the US market.'

key_facts.fact: Hassabis said he published the framework after concerns about the cyber capabilities of Anthropic's Mythos model, which he called a 'warning shot', and that he had socialized the plan with virtually every major AI lab, including Dario Amodei
key_facts.excerpt: Hassabis, who had been preparing his framework for months, said he decided to publish it following concerns around the advanced cybersecurity capabilities of Anthropic's Mythos model, which he called a 'warning shot' for society.

key_facts.fact: The body would be able to evaluate frontier models before release and coordinate an industry-wide slowdown if they were judged too risky, with a majority-independent board and funding from AI firms
key_facts.excerpt: The organization... would be made up of leading independent experts and representatives from open-source communities and would have the authority to evaluate frontier models before they are released and coordinate an industry-wide slowdown if they were judged too risky to deploy.

stories.headline: Experts confirm a 22-year math conjecture fell to a doctor and a 16-hour GPT-5.6 run

key_facts.fact: Michel Crouzeix himself, along with mathematicians Alex Townsend and Anne Greenbaum, checked the proof thoroughly and believe the manuscript is correct, they wrote in an essay for SIAM News that circulated on August 12-13
key_facts.excerpt: Both authors of this article, as well as Michel Crouzeix himself, have checked the proof thoroughly and believe that Dr. Jin's manuscript is correct.

key_facts.fact: The author is Shanmu Jin, a postdoctoral researcher and neurosurgery resident at Peking Union Medical College Hospital who studied geology as an undergraduate and later earned an M.D.; beyond standard science courses, 'everything has been self-taught'
key_facts.excerpt: The author of the preprint is Dr. Shanmu Jin... a postdoctoral researcher and neurosurgery resident at Peking Union Medical College Hospital. He studied geology as an undergraduate and later earned an M.D. His formal mathematical education consisted of the courses ordinarily taken by science students. 'Everything beyond that has been self-taught.'

key_facts.fact: Jin says the key result, Theorem 3.1 of his preprint, emerged during an approximately sixteen-hour autonomous run of GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT Work mode, with no human intervention after he started it
key_facts.excerpt: Jin told us that the key result (see Theorem 3.1 of his preprint) emerged during an approximately sixteen-hour autonomous run of GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT Work mode... Jin then started the run and did not intervene.

key_facts.fact: He adapted a prompt OpenAI used on the Cycle Double Cover conjecture: it denied the model web access, required a branching portfolio of different approaches, told subagents not to converge prematurely, and demanded adversarial audits until a complete proof survived checking
key_facts.excerpt: He adapted a prompt used by OpenAI to solve the Cycle Double Cover conjecture. The prompt explicitly denied the system access to the public web and other external contexts... It told ChatGPT to spin up lots of subagents to individually think about proof strategy, and that these agents should not converge prematurely on the same attractive idea.

key_facts.fact: Crouzeix formulated the conjecture in 2004 and proved in 2007 that a constant of 11.08 sufficed; Crouzeix and Palencia cut it to 1+√2 ≈ 2.414 in 2017. Jin's preprint, 'The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set', was posted July 27, 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Crouzeix formulated it in 2004 and proved in 2007 that replacing the constant 2 in (1) with 11.08 always suffices. In 2017, Crouzeix and Palencia reduced the universal constant to 1 + √2 ≈ 2.414.

key_facts.fact: Eight days later, on August 4, Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger posted an independent five-page proof using a different argument; they also disclose using ChatGPT 5.6 to explore proof strategies
key_facts.excerpt: On August 4—only eight days after Jin's first preprint appeared—Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger posted an independent five-page proof. Their argument is different and strikingly short... Lorist and Schwenninger also disclose that ChatGPT 5.6 was used to explore proof strategies.

key_facts.fact: Jin's public repository includes the prompt, successive manuscripts, a Lean formalization and an axiom audit
key_facts.excerpt: Jin's repository also includes the prompt, successive manuscripts, a Lean formalization, and an axiom audit, which makes the work unusually open to examination.

key_facts.fact: The account spread on X on August 12-13, with users noting the decisive theorem came from a roughly 16-hour autonomous GPT-5.6 Sol run and that Crouzeix has checked the proof
key_facts.excerpt: A neurosurgery resident with little formal advanced math training solved the 20+ year old Crouzeix conjecture (a major open problem in operator theory and matrix analysis) with the decisive theorem emerging from a ~16 hour autonomous GPT-5.6 Sol run.

stories.headline: Twitch says Amazon trains AI on streamers' content by default, adds an opt-out toggle

key_facts.fact: Twitch added a 'Training for Generative AI' setting on August 12 that lets users block their streams, VODs, clips, stream chats and channel images and text from future training of Amazon models that generate text, audio, images or video
key_facts.excerpt: Opting out means that 'your streams, VODs, clips, stream chats, and pictures and text on your channel' won't be used in 'future training' of an Amazon AI model 'whose purpose is to generate or synthesize text, audio, images, or video,' according to a Twitch support page.

key_facts.fact: Creators are opted in by default and must manually opt out, which drove immediate backlash across the Twitch community
key_facts.excerpt: This move has inspired swift and concentrated backlash from the Twitch community, especially because creators are opted in to having their content used for this AI training by default.

key_facts.fact: Twitch chief product officer Mike Minton said the default is deliberate: 'If it was opt in, nobody would opt in. That's honestly the answer'
key_facts.excerpt: 'If it was opt in, nobody would opt in. That's honestly the answer,' he said. 'So it's going to be on by default. And as I said, almost every service in the world is on by default.'

key_facts.fact: Within hours of the announcement, nearly 14,000 people had upvoted a support-forum comment demanding the setting be opt-in instead of opt-out
key_facts.excerpt: Within hours of Twitch's announcement, nearly 14,000 people had upvoted a comment on the company's support forum demanding the platform make the setting opt-in and not opt-out.

key_facts.fact: The change comes more than two years after a Twitch executive publicly confirmed Amazon was already using Twitch content for AI training; Minton said he does not know what has already been used
key_facts.excerpt: The change, announced today, comes more than two years after a company executive confirmed that Amazon was using Twitch content for AI training.

key_facts.fact: Opting out does not disable other AI uses such as AutoMod moderation, captions and recommendations, and chats sent on someone else's stream are governed by that channel owner's preference
key_facts.excerpt: Other 'AI-supported' features like captions and safety tools will still function if you opt out... However, if you participate in a chat on another person's stream, 'their opt-out preferences govern if that chat can be used for training.'

key_facts.fact: Some users reported that after toggling the option off, they returned to settings to find it switched back on
key_facts.excerpt: Some users have since said despite toggling off the option, they have then returned to the settings to find the feature turned on again.
